mechanism_narrative: A lower unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a stronger labor market, which typically supports corporate earnings growth and reduces risk aversion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
evidence_refs: fact:UNRATE at 4.2% is below 5-year average of 4.5%
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE is below 4.0% or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL value above 315 indicates elevated inflation, which typically triggers central bank tightening and increases risk premiums, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances (CPIAUCSL > 315) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL: when the federal funds rate is above 4.5% and CPIAUCSL is above 315, it signals a restrictive monetary policy environment that suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5 AND CPIAUCSL > 315 or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
